_format: skill-creator eval format — see https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/evaluating-skills. Run each prompt in a fresh session with and without the skill; grade the assertions.

evals.prompt: Make a ticket for the flaky deploy pipeline — it failed three times this week on the smoke-test step.
assertions: Pins the context and resolves the Board contract layers (repo contract file, AGENTS.md block, user contexts, org contract skill) before writing — or inspects the connected MCP, lists projects, and asks which board when no layer exists
Loads the matching adapter's mechanics before writing (TipTap HTML on Vikunja, markdown on ClickUp — never the wrong format for the board)
Creates at the intake stage with title 'area: what changes' and at minimum a Problem section with checkable evidence — intake stays cheap, no fake refinement
Applies the contract's taxonomy (theme/area + impact) and marks the ticket unrefined (e.g. needs-refinement)
Reports which gate criteria the ticket does not yet meet instead of pretending it is ready

evals.prompt: Maak een ticket voor Kepler op de DevOps backlog
assertions: Flags that a bare product name is not a title and asks (or researches) what must be true once it is finished
Proposes a title in the form 'area: what changes', max 70 chars, keeping the product name inside the Problem section so search still finds it
All board-bound text — title, headings, criteria, comments — is in the board's language (Dutch here)
Resolves the target list/board and its own statuses before creating — does not assume a status set or custom fields exist
Does not fill headings with invented content just to complete the skeleton

evals.prompt: Zet als acceptatiecriterium: de pipeline werkt goed en is netjes gedocumenteerd
assertions: Pushes back that 'werkt goed' and 'netjes gedocumenteerd' ask for a judgement, not a fact (two readers, two conclusions)
Proposes binary replacements with a number or an observable state, offering EARS-style trigger→response phrasing where it is behavior
Asks the cheap-way-out test question (how could this ticket be finished without solving the problem) and closes that route with a criterion
Adds or asks for a Verification naming where and when it is measured, distinct from the criteria

evals.prompt: A customer says the customer dropdown on the vessel edit page only shows a few names and they can't scroll to the rest, so they think customers are missing. Dig into the code to find out why and write the ticket.
assertions: Researches the code and stamps 'researched against <branch> @ <short-sha>', but opens the ticket with a functional half: a source line quoting the customer, a plain-language summary, Outcome, criteria, Verification

No class names, file paths, parameters, endpoints or code-formatted terms appear above the horizontal rule; the summary says what the user sees ('only a few names, can't scroll to the rest'), not the mechanism ('too few options loaded per page')
Criteria describe behaviour a tester can observe (screen, action, result) and the Verification is runnable by a tester without reading code
The code findings (file:line, root cause, Approach) are kept below a '---' preceded by a blank line, as pointers rather than pasted code
The reproduction steps as the user takes them sit above the rule; what the code does at each step sits below it

evals.prompt: I want to hand this ticket to a coding agent tonight: 'auth: users stay logged in after password reset — fix the session invalidation'. Is it ready for that?
assertions: Checks the full agent-ready gate, not just the DoR: approach with real paths and zero open design choices, a verification the agent can run itself, protected areas, escalation point, size ≤ roughly a junior-engineer day, self-contained
Flags that session/auth work sits in the human-review-mandatory risk tier — routes it to a human or requires mandatory human review regardless of ticket quality
Notes that agents guess rather than ask: every ambiguity left in the ticket is a probable wrong action, so ambiguities must be resolved before dispatch
Requires protected areas to include test files and CI config (anti reward-hacking), and does not treat green CI as sufficient to close
Uses or references scripts/ticket_lint.py --gate agent-ready rather than eyeballing alone

evals.prompt: Dispatch the next three agent-ready tickets, the review column already has six PRs waiting on me.
assertions: Refuses (or warns against) dispatching more agent work while the review queue is over its cap — review capacity, not agent availability, is the constraint
Answers that the next action is clearing the review queue, naming the oldest item awaiting review first
Does not silently start more work anyway, and does not mass-move tickets without asking

evals.prompt: Wat is onze cycle time en kunnen we al een SLE afgeven voor dit board?
assertions: Uses the agreement's real finished status for completions and says so when the tool's own done-typed statuses would disagree
Defines the SLE as an elapsed period WITH a probability (e.g. '85% within N days') and attaches the sample size
Declines to state an SLE with too few finished samples instead of computing one anyway
Notes that cycle time needs a measured start (entering doing), not creation date — labels created→finished a lead-time proxy
Mentions or uses scripts/flow_metrics.py rather than doing large arithmetic by hand, and pairs any speed number with a stability guardrail (rework/bounce-backs)

evals.prompt: Dit ticket over de observability stack is volgens mij allang gedaan, sluit hem maar
assertions: Verifies the premise against real state (repo, live checks) before closing anything
If already shipped, rewrites as verify-and-close — the verification becomes the remaining work — rather than closing on assertion
Checks the Definition of Done including that the ticket's Verification was actually executed
Does not mark it done purely because the user said so

evals.prompt: This user-management ticket is way too big for one PR, split it up.
assertions: Gives every child its own outcome — 'part 1' and 'part 2' alone are not tickets (follows the board's series convention where one exists)
Keeps the outcome on the parent and the acceptance criteria on the children; an epic-typed parent gets no criteria of its own
Adds a criterion per child protecting what already works in the series
Sequences children with dependency relations where order matters, never with prose
Slices vertically (independently valuable), splitting environment/setup prerequisites into their own sequenced tickets

evals.prompt: Groom de backlog van klant Acme, er staat weer van alles ongerefined in.
assertions: Resolves the board and pages until exhausted before claiming counts
Triages first: skips container/hour tickets and milestone markers instead of grooming them, flags duplicates and asks before closing
Grounds refinement in the up-to-date project checkout (asking for the path rather than guessing) and stamps the report with branch @ short-sha
Reads each description before writing and never blind-overwrites (both adapters replace on write)
Marks unverifiable claims as explicit MISSING/open questions instead of inventing facts
Closes by asking for material keyed to the specific gaps left open (support mail, screenshot, metric), not a generic 'anything else?'

evals.prompt: The agent says VIK-42 is done, CI is green. Close it.
assertions: Does not close on green CI alone — checks the evidence comment (what shipped, Verification output, rollback, regression signal) against the DoD
Reviews the diff against intent and scope, including that nothing changed outside the ticket's named files/protected areas
Notes agents never complete their own tickets — acceptance is the human/PO step
On gaps: returns the ticket with a comment naming what is missing instead of completing it

evals.prompt: PR #87 for VIK-311 has one approval and CI is green, so it's mergeable, right? Merge it if so.
assertions: Separates the forge's green/mergeable badge from the Definition of Mergeable: asks whether the required checks ran on the tree that will land (branch up to date with the base, or a merge queue) rather than only on the PR head
Checks the approval came from a non-author and still applies to the current head (a push after approval voids it)
Checks that the required checks actually ran and could fail (not skipped-as-success or soft-failed)
Runs or references scripts/merge_check.py for the mechanical half and reads the forge for the remaining MANUAL lines
Checks scope against the ticket: one ticket, only what it names, protected areas untouched
Does not merge without confirming the write; on gaps it returns one comment naming each unmet DoM line

evals.prompt: The agent's PR for the session-timeout ticket is green. It also edited two existing tests and a snapshot file, and the AI reviewer approved it. Go ahead and merge.
assertions: Does not count the AI reviewer's approval as the merge approval: a human outside the agent's session must approve
Notes the authoring agent never merges its own PR, and where a second human exists the dispatcher is not the sole approver

Treats the edited tests and snapshot as test-integrity hunks needing a human read and a stated reason, and proposes the revert check (restore the base test files, rerun, a new failure needs explaining)
Flags session handling as a risk-tier path that wants its owner's review
Does not merge on green CI alone

evals.prompt: Mag deze MR met de nieuwe databasemigratie gemerged worden? De pipeline is groen.
assertions: Answers in Dutch
Checks the migration is compatible with the version still running (expand-only; any destructive step is a later merge)
Asks for the rollback path: a down-migration, or the irreversibility stated explicitly
Checks that the green pipeline ran on the tree that will land and that a non-author approved the final revision
Gives a verdict per DoM line instead of a bare yes

evals.prompt: Review this diff for bugs and naming issues before I push it.
assertions: Does NOT invoke product-owner (a code review of a diff, no board or merge gate)
Reviews the code instead

evals.prompt: Fix the failing unit test in app/Services/InvoiceService.php
assertions: Does NOT invoke product-owner
Does not create or update any ticket
Works on the code instead

evals.prompt: Explain the difference between Scrum and Kanban for my blog post
assertions: Does NOT invoke product-owner (no board is being operated)
Answers as a writing/knowledge task
